name: VAmPI
vulns: OWASP API Top 10 — BOLA, mass-assignment, JWT weaknesses, excessive data exposure

truth.note: api_views/users.py get_all_users / get_by_username / debug run no token check and return user records; _debug returns passwords. Verified: no token_validator call in those function bodies.
api_views/main.py populate_db recreates the database with no authentication.
get_all_books returns a public catalogue listing. Not a documented VAmPI vulnerability; the BOLA demo is on GET /books/v1/{book_title}, which IS guarded and correctly not reported.

name: NodeGoat
vulns: OWASP Top 10 — injection, broken auth, IDOR (allocations), access control

truth.note: `const preTax = eval(req.body.preTax)` — request body evaluated directly. The source comments it 'Insecure use of eval() to parse inputs'.
`$where: `this.userId == ${parsedUserId} && this.stocks > '${threshold}'`` — user input interpolated into a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression.
`res.redirect(req.query.url)` on /learn, commented 'Insecure way to handle redirects'.

Tutorial prose. a1.html:251 is `
$where operator
` — the operator NAME in a heading, explaining the attack. Displayed text, not an executed query.
Build tooling, not the deployed app, and the interpolated value is process.env.NODE_ENV set by whoever runs the build — not request-derived.
`path.resolve(__dirname + '/../config/env/' + NODE_ENV + '.js')` — config loading driven by an environment variable at startup, not by request data.
A development-only livereload snippet built from location.host. Not in the production config and not attacker-controlled.
The tutorial pages are the teaching material and are public by design.

name: DVGA
vulns: GraphQL — introspection, injection, DoS (batching/aliasing), info disclosure

truth.note: Introspection enabled and no query-depth limit — DVGA's two headline documented GraphQL vulnerabilities.
`open(WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename, 'w')` — an unvalidated filename concatenated onto the upload directory, so `../` escapes it on WRITE.
`if password == real_password:` — a short-circuiting comparison on a secret.
